literal: The ruin of him who holds anger as a valuable thing is like the hand of him who struck the ground not failing to hurt.
translation: The ruin of one who cherishes anger as a valuable thing is as certain and unavoidable as the pain felt in the hand of someone who strikes the ground.
modern: கோபத்தை ஒரு சிறந்த குணமாகக் கொண்டு அதை வளர்ப்பவனுடைய அழிவானது, தரையைத் தன் கையால் அடித்தவனுடைய கைக்கு வலி ஏற்படுவது தப்பாது என்பதைப் போன்றது.
explanation: This couplet illustrates the self-destructive nature of anger using a vivid, everyday physical analogy. The poet compares harboring anger to striking the ground with one's bare hand. Just as the ground remains unharmed while the hand that strikes it inevitably suffers pain, the person who holds onto anger only ends up destroying themselves rather than hurting the object of their anger. The key word 'பொருள்' (meaning a valuable asset or reality) shows how foolish it is to treat a destructive emotion like anger as something worth holding onto.
